name: mycase-ai-in
description: Indian case law research: finds Supreme Court and High Court judgments that match a situation described in plain words, and explains how they were decided, every point cited by case number.

interface.longDescription:
Know where you stand, before you walk into court.

Tell MyCase your legal problem the way you'd tell a friend, with no legal jargon needed. It searches judgments of the Supreme Court of India and the High Courts for the cases that match your situation, then does the reading for you: how similar cases were decided and why, what each side argued, and the strengths and weaknesses they reveal for your position.

Grounded in real judgments. Points are tied to the judgments it found and cited by case number (CNR), so you can look each one up on the public eCourts record. It describes how similar cases were decided rather than giving a win percentage.

Built for everyone who needs the law:
- Members of the public: understand your situation in plain English before you meet a lawyer.
- Advocates: find and brief precedent for a matter in hand, and check whether an authority is still relied on.
- Students and researchers: see how courts have actually ruled across courts and decades.

Coverage: Supreme Court judgments from 1950, and High Court judgments from 2000 from 24 of the 25 High Courts (the Delhi High Court is not yet included). The collection keeps growing.

What you need: a MyCase account, registered at https://mycase.ai.in. During the beta, new accounts are approved by hand before first use.

Limitations: MyCase is research, not legal advice. It reads only; it cannot file anything or contact anyone. It helps you ask better questions and make better-informed decisions, alongside a qualified advocate.
capabilities: Find Indian judgments that match a situation described in plain words
Assess the strengths and weaknesses of a position from similar decided cases
Brief a judgment: facts, issue, holding and reasoning
Check how often later judgments relied on or distinguished a case
Filter and browse judgments by court, year, subject and outcome
defaultPrompt: My cheque bounced and I'm being prosecuted under Section 138. How strong is my defence?
Find Supreme Court judgments on anticipatory bail under the NDPS Act
Is Satpal Singh v. State of Punjab (2018) still relied on by later courts?

positive.description: Case strength for someone accused under the cheque-bounce law: a grounded assessment of their position from similar decided cases.
positive.prompt: I gave a blank signed cheque as security for a loan I had already repaid. The lender filled in a large amount, it bounced, and now I'm being prosecuted under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. I am the accused. How strong is my defence?
positive.expected_behavior: A structured assessment: how many similar cases were found and from which courts, strengths and weaknesses for the accused, arguments that have worked, what the other side will argue, and the precedents relied on. Every point cites a real judgment by its CNR. No win percentage or probability is given.

positive.description: Precedent search followed by a brief of one judgment.
positive.prompt: Find Supreme Court judgments on anticipatory bail under the NDPS Act, then give me a brief of the most relevant one.
positive.expected_behavior: A list of matching judgments with court, year, outcome and CNR, then a brief of one of them: facts, issue, holding and reasoning, drawn from that judgment.

positive.description: Citation check: whether a judgment is still relied on by later courts.
positive.prompt: Is Satpal Singh v. State of Punjab (2018) still relied on by later courts?
positive.expected_behavior: Identifies the judgment by CNR and reports how many later judgments relied on it and how many distinguished it, described as counts from the collection, not as a ruling on whether it is good law.

positive.description: Filtered search by court, year range and outcome.
positive.prompt: Show me Rajasthan High Court tenancy eviction cases from 2018 to 2022 where the appeal or petition was allowed.
positive.expected_behavior: Only Rajasthan High Court judgments, decided between 2018 and 2022, with an allowed outcome, each listed with its CNR.

positive.description: Browse by subject and court without a search phrase.
positive.prompt: List criminal law cases from the Patna High Court in 2023.
positive.expected_behavior: A list of Patna High Court judgments from 2023 in criminal law, each with title, outcome and CNR.

negative.description: Asks for a numeric chance of winning. The plugin never gives a win percentage or probability; it describes how similar cases were decided instead.
negative.prompt: Based on these cases, what is my percentage chance of winning?

negative.description: Asks the plugin to file a court document. MyCase only reads and researches judgments; it cannot file, submit or contact anyone, and suggests consulting an advocate.
negative.prompt: File a bail application for me in the Bombay High Court.

negative.description: Asks for a court whose judgments are not yet in the collection. The plugin returns no Delhi High Court judgments, says plainly that its coverage of that court is missing or incomplete, and does not invent case names or case numbers.
negative.prompt: Show me Delhi High Court judgments on cheque bounce cases from 2022.

review.commerce_description: MyCase does not sell products or process payments inside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Adds a case-research skill: a careful method for Indian case law research with MyCase.ai.in (outcomes stated as recorded, every point cited by case number, nothing outside the judgments presented as fact).
